page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor delivering 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs at 1 thread per core) clocked at 2.8 GHz, complemented by 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core). Cache allocation comprises 64 KB of L1d, 2 MB of L2, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, includes no local storage, operates without discrete GPUs, and provides a 33 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight solid throughput across memory-intensive and multi-threaded processing tasks. The instance demonstrates strong large-block memory bandwidth (294.53 GB/sec read, 132.58 GB/sec write) and placed in the top 10% for the PassMark memory score (3216.25). Compute-heavy benchmarks show strong multi-core scaling, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 15875.0 and 202.01 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. PassMark database operations also tested in the top 25% at 24174.88 ops. General CPU evaluations, such as Geekbench single-core (1894.0) and stress-ng multi-core (27304.05), register within the middle 50% tier.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, dedicated core layout, and high baseline networking provide strong resource efficiency for scaled horizontal workloads. While it lacks local NVMe disks and specialized AVX/AMX instruction support, its high memory throughput and 16 dedicated ARM cores make it well suited for web serving, microservices, compilation pipelines, database engines, and continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) environments.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 16-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 33 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies purely on remote storage, containing no bundled local drives or GPU accelerators. Benchmark analysis demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving high uncached read and write throughput alongside top-decile PassMark memory results. Multi-threaded processing capabilities are strong, evident in multi-core Geekbench and compression metrics. Single-core compute and extended instruction tests fall into mid-range tiers, reflecting its balanced Neoverse-V2 efficiency. Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio and high networking throughput, c8gb.4xlarge is well positioned for containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation workloads, backend web serving, and distributed database services.
